stories.title: Two-day consultation on One Health - Antimicrobial Resistance Action Plan for Tamil Nadu held
stories.summary: A total of 105 officials from 19 departments came together for a two-day consultation on the development of One Health - Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Action Plan for Tamil Nadu. 0. It was organised on November 23 and 24, according to a social media post by the Directorate of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

stories.title: Maharashtra FDA cancels Inducare’s manufacturing licences again over nine unauthorised drugs, two found spurious
stories.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) said it had cancelled the drug manufacturing licences of Pune-based Inducare Pharmaceutical and Research Foundation for the second time after the firm was found to have manufactured and sold nine drugs without mandatory product permission, all of which were subsequently declared substandard, misbranded or spurious by government analysts.

stories.title: Hospital launches maternity and fertility centre
stories.summary: Dr. G. Viswanathan Hospitals launched AIRA – Complete Women Care, Maternity and IVF, a centre offering women’s healthcare and maternity services at Mambalasalai, Tiruchi, on Wednesday. AIRA will offer comprehensive gynaecological, women’s healthcare and maternity services, bringing together reproductive health, pregnancy care and fertility services under one roof.

stories.title: Breastfeeding beyond 10 months statistically linked to higher blood pressure in children: Report
stories.summary: The best start to a newborn’s life is to give them exclusive breastfeeding for at least the initial six months, the World Health Organisation (WHO) has advised. Many parents may continue feeding them for longer, a year or two or even more. For most part, breastfeeding has been associated with good nutrition and immunity for the baby.

stories.title: Raj orders statewide crackdown on quack doctors
stories.summary: The drive will be carried out with the support of local administration and police to ensure effective enforcement. The Indian Medical Association (IMA) had sent multiple representations to the state govt, flagging the widespread presence of unauthorised practitioners and warning that their interventions were causing serious complications among patients.

stories.title: India v New Zealand Test: Shubman Gill’s character as captain on Test
stories.summary: Shubman Gill would be left with bitter recollections of having to close back-to-back Tests with part-timers Dhruv Jurel and Yashasvi Jaiswal. Even though momentarily it is all fun and games when batters are bowling dollies to bring a closure to a no-result Test, in effect, it means the bowlers have conceded their inability to force a victory.

stories.title: Glenn makes 'free ball' history in WBBL after Dottin timed out
stories.summary: Watch the moment England's Sarah Glenn makes history in the women's Big Bash League as she bowls at an empty set of stumps with a 'free ball', to dismiss Deandra Dottin after the batter was ruled to have taken too long to face the delivery.

stories.title: AITA elections on November 27, but results to be remain in abeyance
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court, on Thursday (November 26, 2026), ordered that the results of the All India Tennis Association (AITA) elections scheduled to be held on November 27 in Ahmedabad be kept in a sealed cover until the next date of hearing, which falls on December 14.

stories.title: Passenger performs puja inside train's AC coach; Railways seeks details
stories.summary: A train journey in India often brings together people from different regions, cultures and religious backgrounds. Sometimes we see passengers carrying their Laddo Gopal, some can be seen with their entire puja samagri. But when an individual activity compromises the safety of everyone on board, it becomes a matter of concern.

stories.title: 2036 Olympics bid: India to make presentation to IOC
stories.summary: Union sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya and outgoing Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha will head the country’s delegation that will discuss India's 2036 Olympic bid with officials of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) on Thursday.

stories.title: Knee surgery rules Sinner out of Australian Open
stories.summary: Jannik Sinner has been ruled out of the Australian Open in January following an operation on his knee. The 25-year-old Italian, who won the 2024 and 2025 titles at Melbourne Park, has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July.

stories.title: Cristiano Ronaldo deserves to leave on his own terms: Pep Guardiola urges Portugal to arrange farewell
stories.summary: The manner in which Cristiano Ronaldo brought his international career to an end has not gone down well with his fans and several former football greats. The Portuguese star called time on his career without a farewell match, following an ugly fallout with manager Jorge Jesus during the national team's camp.

stories.title: Champions League: Man United and PSG held to draws, Bayern loses
stories.summary: Mauricio Pochettino was denied his first win as Manchester United coach in calamitous circumstances after a 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League. Paris Saint-Germain was held to the same scoreline by Roma, ending the back-to-back defending champion's 100% winning record and leaving Real Madrid out in front at the top of the standings.

stories.title: SMAT: UP thrashed by Bengal
stories.summary: Former champions Uttar Pradesh edged closer to elimination in the T20 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy after Bengal inflicted a 93-run defeat in them in Mumbai on Tuesday. Bengal dismantled them, posting 201/3 in 15 overs and then restricting UP to 108/7. The match aggregate of just 309 runs was the lowest in a T20 involving Bengal and Uttar Pradesh, but Bengal owned the contest from the start.

stories.title: Fifa confirms internal data stolen in cyber attack
stories.summary: Football issues correspondent Published 6 minutes ago Fifa has confirmed it has been the victim of a cyber attack which resulted in personal and business information being stolen. However, BBC Sport understands the data breach did not include any documents relating to the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, president Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plot.

stories.title: IND vs NZ second Test: Morne Morkel urges patience with Anshul Kamboj’s performance
stories.summary: Anshul Kamboj may have had an underwhelming start to his Test career, but India bowling coach Morne Morkel has urged patience with the young fast bowler, insisting that it would be premature to pass judgement after just two Tests on largely unresponsive surfaces. Kamboj, who made his debut during the England tour last year, returned figures of one for 89 at Old Trafford.

stories.title: Khasdar Krida Sangram Season 2 Enters Final Stretch Ahead Of Grand Finale On November 29
stories.summary: The ten-day sporting extravaganza, featuring over 75,000 athletes across 30+ disciplines, will culminate in a grand closing ceremony on Sunday, November 29, celebrating the district’s emerging champions. Organised by the Dr. Shrikant Shinde Foundation on the initiative of Kalyan MP Dr. Shrikant Eknath Shinde, under the guidance of Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde, the festival aligns with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Sansad Khel Mahotsav vision.

stories.title: Abhishek Sharma scores 37-ball fifty against Sri Lanka A in Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 semifinal
stories.summary: India A’s Abhishek Sharma scored a half-century against Sri Lanka A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars semifinal in Doha on Thursday. The Punjab opener’s knock, comprising nine fours, put India in a position of command in the semifinal. Abhishek first combined with Vaibhav Sooryvanshi in the Powerplay to keep the scoreboard ticking with regular boundaries.

stories.title: 'He won’t be joining': Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open; here's why
stories.summary: “Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. ”Sinner said on Tuesday that he had undergone a “minor” operation on his right knee after other treatments failed to resolve the problem. The Italian has not played since successfully defending his Wimbledon title in July, which gave him his fifth Grand Slam singles trophy.

stories.title: Leaked FIFA documents show Infantino’s 96-year private equity plan for World Cup
stories.summary: The leaked documents, including a FIFA in-house risk assessment, show its own finance officials “were not directly privy to the construction of this transaction”

stories.title: United States lined up to co-host 2034 men’s T20 World Cup with West Indies
stories.summary: The United States is being lined up to co-host the 2034 men’s T20 World Cup in a joint enterprise with West Indies. The International Cricket Council announced the dates of all global events until 2035 after their quarterly meeting in Bali last week, but has not confirmed any venues beyond the 50-over World Cup in 2031 in India and Bangladesh.

stories.title: India, New Zealand eye series win at Hagley Oval as WTC stakes add spice to Christchurch Test
stories.summary: India and New Zealand will look to settle their opening-Test stalemate when they meet in the second and final match of the series at Hagley Oval from Friday, with both teams hoping for a more sporting surface and India particularly keen to strengthen their World Test Championship (WTC) final prospects.

stories.title: IND A vs SL A, Rising Stars Asia Cup Semi-Final: Abhishek Sharma Gets Lucky! Sri Lanka Captain Pavan Rathnayake Drops Regulation Catch At Covers | Video
stories.summary: Sri Lanka A captain Pavan Rathnayake had an embarrassing moment on the field after dropping a straightforward catch of India's explosive opener Abhishek Sharma during the Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026 semi-final on Thursday. The Sri Lankan skipper failed to hold on to a regulation chance at cover, handing the Indian batter a crucial lifeline.

stories.title: How Rajasthan Royals missed once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to acquire Hardik Pandya
stories.summary: Ever since Mumbai Indians (MI) played their last league match of IPL 2026, speculation was rife over Hardik Pandya's future. Multiple teams were in the race to sign the flamboyant all-rounder, whose second stint with MI, having returned to the franchise in the 2024 season as captain, replacing long-serving skipper Rohit Sharma, didn't go as planned.

stories.title: World chess championship: Gritty Gukesh weathers time pressure, holds Sindarov
stories.summary: There was this man-against-machine match in chess in 1998. If you thought the machine might have won, you are wrong. The man, named Viswanathan Anand, beat Fritz. The computer had white pieces and it opted for the Spanish Game. Anand, who hadn’t yet won any of his World titles yet, played the Berlin Defence.

stories.title: Khawaja: Never expected Pat to come out and attack me personally
stories.summary: Australia opener Usman Khawaja has revealed that he was left deeply hurt by Pat Cummins' explosive press conference addressing the infamous 2018 Sandpapergate scandal. Khawaja admitted that he never expected the Australian captain to personally attack him while responding to allegations made in his recently released autobiography, Sabr.

stories.title: Snooker 900: Pankaj Advani becomes first Indian to win Crucible Cup
stories.summary: K. Advani, the reigning world billiard champion, displayed a blend of skill and composure to beat defending champion and former world snooker champion Neil Robertson of Australia 5-2 in his first match. In his next encounter, the Indian made light work of the challenge of Joe Perry 5-1 to book his place in the final.

stories.title: Vedant Sehwag bags seven-wicket haul for brother Aaryavir-led Delhi vs Punjab
stories.summary: In a remarkable display of skill, Vedant Sehwag secured a stunning seven-wicket haul for Delhi U-19 in their match against Punjab U-19 during the Cooch Behar Trophy. His standout performance was instrumental in Delhi's triumph, aided by Nakul Yadav and others. This achievement not only reinforces the Sehwag cricket legacy but also signifies a promising chapter in Vedant's budding career, echoing the excellence of his father.

stories.title: AITA presidential election: Chintan Parekh vs Rohit Rajpal - two visions for Indian tennis
stories.summary: Chintan Parekh and Rohit Rajpal are pitching contrasting visions for Indian tennis as they vie for the All India Tennis Association (AITA) presidency. Both promise player-centric reforms and greater support, but their approaches differ. The AITA elections will take place on Friday.

stories.title: Sahiba Bali's Gurpurab post with Arjun Kapoor sparks dating buzz, fans wonder 'is it a soft launch?'
stories.summary: Dating lives of celebrities are something every entertainment junkie is deeply interested in. And, with the strong presence of social media, fans often get to know about the whereabouts of their favourite actors. Something similar happened recently when actor and sports presenter Sahiba Bali uploaded a photo with actor Arjun Kapoor.

stories.title: India's top court tightens food warning labels in ne
stories.summary: NEW DELHI, - India's top court ruled on Thursday that separate warning labels should appear on the front of food packaging for every nutrient of concern, tightening a government proposal that called for a single label and dealing a blow to the $100 billion industry that has long opposed the measure.

stories.title: Why India is betting Rs 11,000 crore on construction, infrastructure equipment manufacturing - explained
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet has approved an Rs 11,000-crore scheme to strengthen India's construction and infrastructure equipment (CIE) manufacturing ecosystem, with a focus on increasing domestic production, supporting component makers and setting up a dedicated testing facility.The decisions were announced by Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw at a press briefing following the Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.The Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment Manufacturing Ecosystem will be implemented by the Ministry of…

stories.title: Knowledge Nugget | EPFO’s new rules explained: From easier PF withdrawals to payout plan for retirees
stories.summary: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), at the meeting of its Central Board of Trustees (CBT) on November 19, 2026, approved key changes to Provident Fund (PF) withdrawal rules. These include reducing the waiting period for final PF settlement after unemployment from 12 months to two months, lowering the minimum balance that members must retain in their accounts from 25% to 10%, and introducing a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP).

stories.title: In a nation of chai drinkers, Darjeeling’s prized tea is a sliver of the crop. Its history and troubles | HT Explainers
stories.summary: Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said last week the government was working to restore the glory of Darjeeling tea – the first Indian product to win a geographical indication (GI) tag – at a time when the hills are growing less tea than they did a generation ago and the industry is struggling.

stories.title: Why has the FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri? | Explained
stories.summary: On November 22, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), the country’s apex food-safety regulator, sanctioned prosecution against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International Pvt. Ltd. after a sample of its water was found to be non-compliant with prescribed safety standards, with the regulator declaring it unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

stories.title: Maharashtra's new property card plan: What flat owners, homebuyers need to know
stories.summary: The Maharashtra government has proposed issuing separate property cards for individual flats in buildings, recording ownership details, sanctioned area, associated rights, mortgages and other liabilities. The proposed system, called the Vertical Property Card, aims to create an independent supplementary record of rights for every eligible flat or unit, alongside existing land records.

stories.title: Flu and other winter viruses can hit older adults harder – here’s what you need to know
stories.summary: “Put a coat on or you’ll catch a cold.” It is a familiar warning, but it leaves out the most important character in the story, the virus. For older people, there is a further concern. Infections such as flu and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) , a common virus that can cause a runny nose or a cough, are more likely to lead to serious illness in this age group.

stories.title: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra Privacy Display explained: What is it and how it works
stories.summary: Samsung’s Privacy Display is a feature built into the Galaxy S26 Ultra that makes the screen harder to read from the side. With the feature enabled, the display directs more light forward, so text and images are easier to see when you look straight at the phone. How Samsung’s Privacy Display worksSamsung calls the technology behind it Flex Magic Pixel.

stories.title: KPSC recruitment scam in Karnataka: How question papers and answer keys reached candidates ahead of exams | Explained
stories.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has alleged that senior Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) officials, including its then Chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar and Controller of Examinations Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, were involved in leaking question papers and answer keys for the recruitment of 400 veterinary officers. The alleged leak involved a network of commission officials, middlemen and candidates, with crores of rupees changing hands.

stories.title: From refined sugar to jaggery: What you need to know before switching your everyday sweetener
stories.summary: Jaggery is often considered healthier than white sugar, but here are the nutritional differences that may surprise you. Swapping sugar with jaggery feels virtuous. But according to a gut-healthy nutritionist, your body barely notices the difference. In an interview with HT Lifestyle, Rashi Chowdhary, chief nutritionist at Nutrition In Sync, explained the nutritional differences so that you can make an informed decision.

stories.title: What does ₹1.25L monthly budget look like? ‘ ₹30,000 grocery, ₹20,000 grooming’: Noida couple’s expenses go viral
stories.summary: Owning a home does not always mean that monthly expenses are low. 25 lakh every month, even though they own their house and do not have to pay rent. The couple shared a video on Instagram explaining their monthly expenses. Their spending includes groceries, household help, gym memberships , grooming, food and travel.

stories.title: Who qualifies as a journalist? SC to ponder question of protection for scribes
stories.summary: New Delhi, The Supreme Court on Thursday said it will consider who qualifies to be a journalist and whether accredited media persons should enjoy greater protection than self-proclaimed reporters while covering protests. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that journalistic freedom has to be balanced with the administration of public order and law.

stories.title: Who Is Lakshmi Venu And Why Is She Seeking Partition Of TVS Family's Wealth Under Hindu Succession Act?
stories.summary: Industrialist Lakshmi Venu has demanded partition of joint family assets belonging to the Venu Srinivasan branch of the TVS family, intensifying the ongoing dispute over family wealth and succession rights. Lakshmi is the daughter of TVS Group Chairman Emeritus Venu Srinivasan and Tractors and Farm Equipment Limited (TAFE) Chairman Mallika Srinivasan.

stories.title: FSSAI vs Bisleri: What is bromate, how does it impact human body, and can it cause cancer? Explained
stories.summary: A finding by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has put packaged drinking water under scrutiny. FSSAI claimed on November 22 that a sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water failed the lab test as it was found “non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits.” On Sunday, through a social media post, FSSAI informed that it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water".

stories.title: SS Rajamoulis Varanasi release may be pushed to August 2027 due to VFX work? Here’s what we know!
stories.summary: Add as a preferred source on Google SS Rajamouli's upcoming epic Varanasi , starring Mahesh Babu, Priyanka Chopra Jonas and Prithviraj Sukumaran, could see a change in its release schedule. Although the film is currently slated to arrive in cinemas on April 7, 2027, reports suggest that the filmmaker is considering a postponement to allow more time for the visual effects (VFX) work.

stories.title: What led to the re-test of three UGC-NET papers? | Explained
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency (NTA) will re-conduct the UGC-NET for English, sociology, and commerce after receiving complaints of “multiple errors” in the question papers, said an official notification released on August 16. The UGC-NET was held from June 22 to 30 for 87 subjects. The notification said the English and commerce papers will be re-conducted on September 9, while that of sociology on September 10.
